brand_identity.status: Owner direction, 2026-07-30: an explicit, permanent identity guardrail that every title, thumbnail, scene choice, audio mood, and Short must reinforce — not a one-time style note to skim past. The niche itself is unchanged (motivational luxury ambient/manifestation content); this codifies the *emotional register* every output must land in.
brand_identity.core_feeling: "This is the life I'm working towards." Every output should make the viewer feel like the video represents the life they want, not just show them a scene.
never: generic hustle-bro/grind-at-all-costs motivation with no luxury/calm framing
aggressive or angry tone in titles/copy
anything that reads as a stock-photo caption or scene description rather than an emotional hook
cheap/gimmicky clickbait that oversells what the video actually is (still bound by shared_gates.platform_policy_check's no-mismatch rule)
brand_identity.reconciling_short_form_energy: Short-form's fast-cut editing pace and upbeat audio tempo (see short_form_style_guidance below) are retention/pacing mechanics, not a brand-identity contradiction — keep the cuts fast, but the *emotional register* of the title, sound choice, and hook must still land in the 'always' list above, not generic aggressive hustle-grind. This also lines up with real performance data already on file (see state/performance_notes.json's 2026-07-29 finding: the channel's own top-performing shorts used calmer, confident-but-not-aggressive tracks, while the two bottom performers both used the most aggressive phonk) — so this isn't just a branding preference, it's also the direction the data points.
brand_identity.self_check_question: Before finalizing any title, thumbnail, or scene: would a viewer feel 'this represents the life I want' — calm, wealthy, disciplined, at peace — or does it just describe what's on screen? If the latter, rewrite it. See config/gates.json's content_quality_gate (the 'Curiosity Engine') for the scored version of this check.

target_audience.core_avatar: A 19-year-old university student or young professional who goes to the gym, listens to ambient or phonk music, spends time on YouTube Shorts and TikTok, wants to become more disciplined, sometimes feels isolated or uncertain about the future, and actively looks for content that helps them grow mentally and emotionally.
share_triggers: This is exactly how I feel.

weekly_batch_mode.description: As of 2026-07-27, the owner requested a fully autonomous weekly batch: every Monday, script/produce/gate all 21 shorts and 7 long-form videos for that week in one cycle, then upload all of them immediately but with YouTube's scheduled-publish feature (privacyStatus=private + publishAt) so they actually go live spread across the week at the slot times below, rather than all going public on Monday. See agents/0_orchestrator.md 'Weekly batch cycle' for the full operating logic.
weekly_batch_mode.slot_time_note: Local times in the timezone above (Europe/London); convert to UTC accounting for BST/GMT when computing each video's publishAt timestamp. Long-form is scheduled after the day's 3rd short so a viewer's day has short-form energy first, calm ambient content in the evening.
weekly_batch_mode.batch_scale_warning: 28 full pipeline cycles (scout->script->produce->gate->publish) in a single run is a large amount of work — real risk of hitting session/token/time limits mid-batch (this has already happened once in a much smaller single-day session). The weekly trigger fires into a persistent, pre-existing session that already has repo access (a fresh session per firing was tried first and failed a live test run: it had no repo clone and no add_repo tool available to get one, since MCP/connector tools aren't passed to fresh-session routine firings). state/weekly_batch_progress.json tracks completion per-item so an interrupted run can be resumed from where it left off rather than restarting the whole batch, and sub-agents should be used liberally within the run to keep the parent session's own context budget from being the limiting factor.
weekly_batch_mode.upload_quota_warning: 2026-07-27T21:35Z: uploading ~11 videos within about an hour of wall-clock time hit YouTube's daily upload quota (HTTP 400 uploadLimitExceeded), even though each video's scheduled_publish_at (via the API's publishAt scheduling) was spread across the week — publishAt only controls when a video goes public, not when the upload call itself counts against the daily cap. Fixed by decoupling production (script/produce/gate, no per-day limit) from publishing (throttled to ~4 uploads/day matching shorts_per_day+long_form_per_day, driven by a trigger that now fires daily instead of weekly). See agents/0_orchestrator.md's Weekly batch cycle section for the full two-phase model. UPDATE 2026-07-28: owner tightened the publish window from 24-48h to a strict next-24h window — each daily firing publishes exactly that day's 3 shorts + 1 long-form and nothing pulled forward from a later day, repeating identically every day. See agents/0_orchestrator.md Weekly batch cycle PUBLISHING phase for the exact rule.

operating_budget: Claude Pro subscription usage only; no paid third-party APIs
human_approval_note: No manual approval step exists in this pipeline. Automatic gates (config/gates.json) replace human review. Gates are never weakened to hit the publishing schedule; failing items are quarantined and the next candidate is selected instead.

short_form_style_guidance.pacing: Fast cuts locked to the actual beat of the audio track (real beat detection, not a fixed-interval grid), HARD CAP of 1.5 seconds per individual shot regardless of beat spacing (tightened from 2.0s per owner direction, 2026-07-27). Pick upbeat/fast-tempo audio deliberately BECAUSE it drives the cut pace — a faster song produces closer-together beats and therefore quicker, more energetic cuts; a slow track would force fewer/slower cuts even with the cap in place. Total video length is now 8-12 seconds (tightened from ~27s per owner direction, 2026-07-27) — at that length a video is roughly 6-9 distinct cuts, not 18-20. The audio's own slow/quiet intro is detected and skipped so playback opens on the real hook/drop, not a build-up — a viewer scrolling onto the Short should land on the energetic part immediately.
short_form_style_guidance.energy: Fast-cut pacing stays as described above — that's a retention mechanic, not a brand contradiction. But as of 2026-07-30 (owner direction, and reinforced by the channel's own performance data — see brand_identity.reconciling_short_form_energy above), the *emotional register* of the audio/hook must land in the luxury/calm/quiet-confidence identity, not generic aggressive hustle-grind. In practice: confident, driving, mid-tempo tracks (not necessarily slow, but not maximally aggressive phonk/hardtekk either) generally fit better than the most aggressive trap/drill options — sound_direction should default toward the calmer end of the 'upbeat' range unless a specific candidate genuinely calls for more intensity. Still NEVER use fully slow ambient/piano/meditation/rain tracks for short-form — those belong to long-form only; the cut pace must still be fast regardless of audio energy level.
short_form_style_guidance.visual_grade: Dark, moody, low-exposure color grade ('gymcore' aesthetic) — reduced brightness/exposure, boosted contrast, slightly desaturated or cool-toned. This is a real, currently-trending look for this niche, not just a preference.
short_form_style_guidance.text_rules: NO on-screen text/captions — dropped entirely per owner direction (2026-07-27). This is a pure visual+audio edit; the title/description carry the message instead.

title_convention.status: Owner direction, 2026-07-30: the previous title approach was too descriptive of the scene itself. Titles must now create an emotional response or curiosity, not describe what's on screen.
title_convention.pattern: The viewer should feel like the title represents the life they want. Evoke: ambition, wealth, peace, success, discipline, manifestation, luxury, quiet confidence, escapism. A title should make someone curious before they even see the thumbnail.
title_convention.banned_pattern: Never write a title that merely describes the scenery/subject (e.g. 'Marina Skyline at Night', 'Luxury Car in the Rain', 'Villa at Sunset'). If the title could function as a stock-photo caption, rewrite it.
good_examples: This Is What Peace Feels Like
Live the Life You Keep Imagining
Become the Person You Dream About
Luxury Is a State of Mind
title_convention.note: This applies on top of, not instead of, the existing hook-driven approach in agents/short_form/1.1_trend_scout.md/2.1_scriptwriter.md — a good `angle` still matters, but the `title` itself must pass the banned_pattern check above regardless of how the angle was framed.

short_form_style_guidance.sources_note: Based on live web research into trending gym/motivation/phonk shorts content and general 2026 YouTube Shorts editing/retention best practices — see state/performance_notes.json for the full findings and sources.

long_form_style_guidance.pacing: Slow, calm, minimal/no cuts — a single looping ambient scene, not edited for pace at all.
long_form_style_guidance.energy: Calm, ambient, meditative. Slow piano/pad/rain/nature tracks belong here, never in short-form.
long_form_style_guidance.visual_grade: Warm or cool moody ambient tones per the scene (rain-on-window, fireplace, etc.), not the dark low-exposure short-form grade — long-form should read as a calm background, not an energetic edit.

title_convention.still_true_from_2026-07-27: Short (3-7 words), punchy, standalone statement someone could say out loud — no duration, no format descriptor, no pipe-separated SEO subtitle, no 'Ambience for Focus & Manifestation' boilerplate, no video-length mention. seo_description and tags still carry the keyword-rich/searchable content (duration, mood, use-case like 'study with me' or 'deep focus').
